articles.title: Dick’s Sporting Goods slumps after earnings miss: What’s next?
articles.excerpt:
Dick’s Sporting Goods shares plunged after the retailer reported weaker-than-expected second-quarter results and cut its full-year outlook. The sharp sell-off reflected growing investor concerns about slowing demand and the challenges facing its recently acquired Foot Locker business. (Sources: The Motley Fool, CNBC)

Dick’s Sporting Goods reported second-quarter revenue of about $5.59 billion, below Wall Street expectations of roughly $5.64 billion. Adjusted earnings per share came in at $3.53, also missing estimates of around $3.76 to $3.78. The earnings shortfall added to concerns about the retailer’s growth outlook.

articles.title: Govt lifts wheat export ban with immediate effect
articles.excerpt:
In February, the government had allowed limited shipments of wheat. | Photo Credit: REUTERS/AMIT DAVE

The government has lifted the export ban on wheat, including the Durum variety grain, with immediate effect.

The government has allowed exports of wheat flour and other products like maida and semolina, according to notifications of the Directorate General of Foreign Trade.

In February, the government had allowed limited shipments of wheat.

"The export policy of wheat....is revised from prohibited to free with immediate effect," one of the notifications stated.

articles.title: Euro zone yields dip from multi-year highs as oil falls on Iran sanctions
articles.excerpt:
On Tuesday, government bond yields across the Euro zone saw a drop from recent peaks, accompanied by falling oil prices as traders evaluated newly imposed U.S. sanctions on Iran. Additionally, money markets adjusted their expectations regarding potential rate hikes by the European Central Bank this year. Meanwhile, recent data highlighted a rebound in German economic growth during the second quarter, with business sentiment climbing to its highest in a year.
